title: Phase 0 context-economy measurement: do fan-out fixed overhead and retries dominate amplification?
summary: Hypothesis: per-worker input-token amplification in orchestrator runs is dominated by fixed fan-out overhead (each worker re-reading the same prompt scaffold and context) and by retries/checkpoint resumes, rather than by task-specific work. Method: run the deterministic, privacy-safe `agent-os orchestrate context-economy` harness read-only over .agent-local/orchestrator/runs, reporting aggregates only (median/p90 input and output amplification per role, long-session context growth ratio, duplicated fan-out overhead, checkpoint-resume overhead share, exact-call coverage), with no prompt or transcript text. Outcome: blocked. The worker's Bash call was denied ('Permission for this tool use was denied. It requires approval, and this session has no approval surface'), so the harness was not run and no numbers exist; the hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted. See EVR-0018. Re-run from a host session.
